## Overview

PTHBV is a database containing daily values of temperature and precipitation over Sweden since 1961.(no content)The main purpose of the database is input for hydrological modeling.

## API Entry Point

Applications that want to benefit from SMHI Open Data PTHBV can use this service to retrieve data.(no content)The entry point is located at `https://opendata-download-metanalys.smhi.se`.

## Data Formats

- **JSON (point/multipoint queries):** The data is returned as mediatype `application/json` (JSON).
- **NetCDF (full grid queries):** The API response is one NetCDF4 file (content-type: `application/x-netcdf`) with the selected values for the entire grid (covering Swedish land).(no content)The projection is RT90 2.5 gon V (EPSG:3021).

## Example API Call

All times are in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time). An example endpoint to get temperature and precipitation analysis at a point near SMHI in Norrköping:

```
https://opendata-download-metanalys.smhi.se/api/category/pthbv1g/version/1/geotype/multipoint/from/2022/to/2023/period/monthly/data.json?epsg=4326&ll=16.158,58.5812&var=p&var=t
```

- **`category`**: `pthbv1g`
- **`version`**: `1`
- **`geotype`**: `multipoint` (for JSON point data)
- **`from`/`to`**: Year range
- **`period`**: e.g. `monthly`
- **`epsg`**: Coordinate reference system (e.g. `4326` for WGS84)
- **`ll`**: Longitude, Latitude
- **`var`**: Variable (`p` for precipitation, `t` for temperature)

- Full API docs: [https://opendata.smhi.se/apidocs/pthbv/](https://opendata.smhi.se/apidocs/pthbv/)

There is also a community Python package (`smhi-open-data`) available on PyPI, though it is geared toward station-based meteorological observations rather than the PTHBV gridded dataset.
